summary: Quarterly business review focused on usage trends, cost drivers, reliability incidents, and roadmap alignment. Solaris is evaluating a Dedicated capacity commit to reduce unit costs; security asks around SOC 2, KMS integration, and audit logs persist. Next actions: pricing, benchmark, security docs, and run a pilot canary for a high-volume route.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for joining the QBR today. we've got about 45 minutes. quick intros, i'm Alex from Redwood, Priya our SE, Leah CSM. Emma?
[00:12] Emma Liu: Hi all, Emma here, thanks. we got Raj, Sarah and Tom on from infra.
[00:18] Raj Patel: Yup, thanks for running this.
[00:20] Priya Reddy: Awesome, we'll jump into usage and then reliability, cost, and next steps. sound good?
[00:25] Emma Liu: Yup.
[01:05] Alex Moreno: Quick stat: your prod token usage has grown ~38% qtr over qtr, embeddings calls up 2x with search feature. main question is, we're seeing cost creep on a few high-throughput routes, want to understand tradeoffs.
[01:30] Tom Alvarez: Yeah, that's the pain. The search embedding pipeline spikes in EU region during morning window. peak tokens/sec is around 7200 for that route.
[01:43] Priya Reddy: Ok that helps. are you currently using caching or prefix KV cache for the search completions?
[01:51] Tom Alvarez: We have simple in-app caching, but not the Redwood prefix cache. we haven't enabled continuous batching either.
[02:05] Emma Liu: Also curious about Dedicated vs Hosted cost math. our finance team wants predictability.
[02:15] Alex Moreno: Totally. dedicated (reserved) gives predictable throughput and lower per-token costs; hosted gives flexibility and simpler ops. We'll send a committed capacity model with breakpoints.
[02:35] Raj Patel: One thing: we have regulatory constraints in APAC for PHI, might need private deployment for a subset.
[02:45] Leah Chen: Noted. Redwood Private (private control plane) supports VPC and on-prem in those cases, with KMS/HSM options.
[02:58] Sarah Gomez: On security, we need SOC 2 Type II evidence, audit log retention options (7 years?), and ability to route logs to our Splunk. Also SSO/SAML and RBAC for team roles.
[03:15] Alex Moreno: We have SOC2 docs and can share them; audit log exports and S3 delivery are supported, plus SSO. we'll share checklist.
[03:30] Priya Reddy: Back to performance: we saw 2 small incidents in March - one was higher latency due to a hot KV shard, second was scheduling latency in a shared pool during burst. both had automatic fallback but caused elevated p95 for about 12 minutes.
[03:55] Raj Patel: Can you explain fallback? the app experienced some timeouts.
[04:05] Priya Reddy: We route by policy; when a primary pool is constrained we fallback to a compatible model variant in another pool. This prevents errors but sometimes increases latency. We also offer dedicated lanes for predictable SLOs.
[04:25] Tom Alvarez: That explains the spikes. If we go dedicated, does that remove fallback behavior?
[04:32] Alex Moreno: With dedicated, you can reserve capacity and set canary/burst policies. fallback to hosted can be disabled if you want strict isolation, but then you need to provision buffer for peaks.
[04:46] Emma Liu: Cost question - what levers do we have for cost reduction besides dedicated?
[04:52] Priya Reddy: Batching, KV/prefix caching to avoid re-gen of common prefixes, quantization profiles for the model family, and routing lower-priority requests to smaller variants. Also dynamic batching settings and token limits on user prompts.
[05:10] Raj Patel: Can you quantify savings?
[05:12] Priya Reddy: Typical batching + caching for search can reduce token compute cost 25-40% depending on hit rates. Quantization on supported models can reduce GPU memory and increase throughput, another 15-30% depending on model and accuracy tolerance. We can run a benchmark to show exact numbers for your workload.
[05:35] Alex Moreno: Action plan - we'll run a Solaris-specific benchmark with your sample traffic to show perf and cost for hosted vs dedicated and a quantized variant.
[05:45] Sarah Gomez: Also, we need to validate encryption in transit, at rest, and KMS integration. Do you support customer-managed keys?
[05:55] Leah Chen: Yes, KMS integrations and HSM options available for Private. For hosted we support customer-managed keys for data at rest in many regions. We'll include details.
[06:10] Tom Alvarez: For the benchmark, we want end-to-end including our pre-processor. can Priya's team deploy the agent in our staging?
[06:20] Priya Reddy: Yes, we'll coordinate. we'll need ssh access to a staging node and a short traffic script.
[06:30] Emma Liu: Roadmap questions: any upcoming features that help long tail cost control?
[06:36] Alex Moreno: In next quarter we plan to ship better workload-aware batching heuristics, more aggressive prefix caching analytics, and an autoscaling policy tuned for steady-state low-latency workloads. Also building more model quantization profiles in the catalog.
[06:55] Raj Patel: Timeline?
[06:56] Alex Moreno: Batching heuristics beta in ~6 weeks, quant profiles ongoing with customer pilots. We'll loop you in on the beta.
[07:05] Emma Liu: Great. Any blockers from Redwood's side for the pilot?
[07:10] Leah Chen: We'll need an approved IP/data handling agreement for the pilot in APAC due to data residency.
[07:20] Sarah Gomez: We'll have legal follow up.
[07:25] Alex Moreno: Ok. switching to Qs from last quarter: Leah, you had a note on contract auto-renew?
[07:32] Leah Chen: yes, just confirming renewal windows and committed capacity right-sizing before auto-renew. we recommend a review 30 days prior.
[07:42] Tom Alvarez: On incident root causes, can we get a short RCA for the March events?
[07:48] Priya Reddy: We'll prepare a 1-pager RCA and include mitigations and config changes.
[07:55] Raj Patel: Good.
[10:05] Alex Moreno: Jumping ahead - pricing model: we'll provide three scenarios: pay-as-you-go (hosted), committed monthly for Dedicated with discounts at 3 and 12 month tiers, and private deployment licensing. I'll attach a spreadsheet.
[10:25] Emma Liu: Please include cost per 1M tokens and embedding batch discounts, and dedicated slot pricing.
[10:30] Alex Moreno: Will do.
[12:15] Sarah Gomez: On audit logs, can we get a sample schema of events and retention controls?
[12:22] Leah Chen: Yes, we'll share the schema and options for S3/Splunk forwarders.
[14:40] Tom Alvarez: A small nit: our dev team sometimes saw misattributed speaker labels in transcripts, curious if that impacts audit logs.
[14:50] Alex Moreno: Fireflies transcripts only - audit logs are structured and separate. will not impact.
[16:00] Raj Patel: For the benchmark, can we include both EU and APAC nodes?
[16:06] Priya Reddy: Yes, we'll provision agents in both regions to capture latency differences.
[18:25] Emma Liu: Are there any critical security controls missing from Redwood that would block us?
[18:30] Sarah Gomez: i can say at a high level.. need confirmation on data residency, KMS, SOC2; otherwise looks ok.
[18:40] Leah Chen: We'll provide a compliance packet and an implementation checklist.
[21:00] Alex Moreno: Recap then next steps: Alex send pricing + spreadsheet; Priya schedule and run benchmarks; Leah share SOC2 and audit log schemas; Sarah/legal will review pilot IP terms; Tom provide traffic profile.
[21:25] Raj Patel: timeline seems good.
[21:50] Emma Liu: thanks all.
[22:00] Alex Moreno: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links.
[22:05] Priya Reddy: bye.
